gwf5mAlI7Ug.summary: A 1953 US Navy training film on the basic mechanisms in fire control computers: shafts, gears, cams and differentials. It shows how these mechanical parts compute ship and target firing solutions.
gwf5mAlI7Ug.why: HN treats it as the classic demonstration of how analog mechanical computation works, especially the differential gear section.

gNRnrn5DE58.summary: Machine Thinking traces where mechanical precision comes from, from flat surface plates and the three-plate method up through lathes and early measuring tools. It is the first in a series on recreating the first micrometer.
gNRnrn5DE58.why: HN commenters repeatedly recommend it as a half-hour mini-documentary on how precision is bootstrapped from scratch, relevant to machining and chip manufacturing threads.

gkj_91IJVBk.summary: Vaclav Smil's talk on historic energy transitions and what they imply for climate investment. He argues that transitions are slow, technology improves gradually, and only absolute cuts in energy use would truly work.
gkj_91IJVBk.why: Frequently linked as a sobering, data-grounded counterpoint to techno-optimism about decarbonization and green growth.

gSPNRu4ZPvE.summary: A short film from Agenda Gotsch introducing syntropic agriculture and Ernst Gotsch's agroforestry methods, made for COP21. It shows degraded land regenerated into productive forest farms.
gSPNRu4ZPvE.why: HN users repeatedly offer it as the best introduction to agroforestry as a climate and food solution.

gCWtkvDQ2ZI.summary: Paul Chiusano's Strange Loop 2019 talk introduces Unison, an open-source functional language for distributed, elastic systems. It covers content-addressed code identified by hashes of the syntax tree, a codebase manager, and algebraic effects called abilities.
gCWtkvDQ2ZI.why: HN treats it as the best introduction to Unison, with commenters finding hash-addressed immutable code mind-blowing.

gB9n2gHsHN4.summary: 3Blue1Brown explains fractal dimension and shows why many fractals are not strictly self-similar. Self-similarity turns out to be a special case of the broader idea of fractional dimension.
gB9n2gHsHN4.why: It is the standard pointer for a clear, visual explanation of what fractals are, and for correcting the idea that fractal means self-similar.

gcUWTa16Jc0.summary: A two-hour live stream in which Aaron Hsu explains the architecture, design history and aesthetic of Co-dfns, his parallel APL compiler. He walks through the code and the reasoning behind its dense style.
gcUWTa16Jc0.why: HN readers say it changed their view of APL and array languages, with a clear walkthrough of how a compiler can be written in this style.

gbYXBJOFgeI.summary: Cory Doctorow's Talks at Google lecture on the coming civil war over general-purpose computing. He argues that locked-down devices, DRM, and surveillance threaten user control of computers.
gbYXBJOFgeI.why: It is HN's go-to reference whenever device lockdown, DRM, or restrictions on installing software come up, with commenters noting how prescient it was.

gTAghAJcO1o.summary: Alan Kay speaks at the DEMO Founder School session on why real progress takes invention rather than incremental innovation. He argues for problem-oriented thinking and long-term research funding.
gTAghAJcO1o.why: HN commenters treat it as a thought-provoking talk on invention versus innovation, and cite it in discussions of software complexity and startups.

gxAaO2rsdIs.summary: 3Blue1Brown builds toy SIR models to simulate how an epidemic spreads and tests scenarios like social distancing, travel restrictions, central gathering places and quarantine. It was made during the early COVID-19 outbreak.
gxAaO2rsdIs.why: HN pointed to it during 2020 as a digestible, well-made illustration of epidemic dynamics and interventions.

g1ib43q3uXQ.summary: Felienne Hermans's Strange Loop keynote on the history and pedagogy of teaching programming. She questions exploration-only approaches like Logo and discusses research supporting explicit instruction and rote practice.
g1ib43q3uXQ.why: Cited in threads about teaching kids and beginners to code as research-based evidence that explicit instruction beats pure discovery.

gEKSpZPByD0.summary: Sean Carroll's 2013 Fermilab Users Meeting lecture on particles, fields and the future of particle physics. He explains that particles are vibrations in underlying quantum fields and touches on the Higgs, neutrinos and dark matter.
gEKSpZPByD0.why: HN recommends it as the clearest long-form explanation of the everything-is-fields view for non-physicists.

gd5uJ7Nlvvo.summary: Dylan Beattie's conference talk explores the history and mess behind plain text: encodings, Unicode, line endings and the many ways text goes wrong. It argues that the tidy idea of plain text hides a lot of complexity underneath everyday software.
gd5uJ7Nlvvo.why: HN people recommend it as an entertaining, surprisingly deep talk that comes up whenever encodings, mojibake or Unicode are discussed.

g3Ud6mHdhlQ.summary: A Smarter Every Day episode from aboard a nuclear submarine on how the crew makes breathable air. It covers oxygen generation from seawater, oxygen candles and CO2 scrubbing with amine.
g3Ud6mHdhlQ.why: Go-to link when oxygen candles, CO2 capture or submarine air quality come up.

gAk7aX5hksU.summary: Asian Boss interviews Professor Kim Woo-joo of Korea University Guro Hospital about COVID-19 in early 2020. He covers masks, testing, aerosol spread, and South Korea's response.
gAk7aX5hksU.why: In early pandemic threads, HN commenters pointed to it as an uninterrupted, practical expert view from Korea on masks, testing and airborne spread.

gV5obrYaogU.summary: A demo of the Symbolics Graphics Division's S-Packages, a Lisp-based 3D color graphics and animation system from the 1980s. It was later used in developing for the Nintendo 64.
gV5obrYaogU.why: HN cites it as a startling example of how advanced Lisp machine interactive graphics were, often in Lisp and REPL-driven development discussions.

gWVmPtr9O0g.summary: Overdrive 2 by TiTAN, a Sega Mega Drive demo that won first place in the Oldskool competition at Revision 2017. It shows effects and 3D graphics on the stock console.
gWVmPtr9O0g.why: HN plugs it as a favorite example of what skilled demoscene coders can pull out of 30-year-old hardware.

g2tMcMQqSbA.summary: Chris Shore of the Centre for Computing History explains how Colossus was built, how it worked, and how it affected the course of World War II. It is an hour-long museum lecture on the codebreaking computer.
g2tMcMQqSbA.why: HN commenters recommend it as an excellent deep dive on the real Colossus, full of stories about unsung engineers.

gDdq2rIqAlM.summary: A 60 Minutes segment on Luxottica, the company that owns most major eyewear brands and retailers and dominates the market. It shows how consolidation of brands and manufacturing affects glasses prices.
gDdq2rIqAlM.why: HN repeatedly cites it in any thread on why glasses are expensive, as the eye-opening explanation of Luxottica's monopoly.

gJ5KV3rzuag.summary: A PBS Space Time episode asking whether Venus would be a better colonization target than Mars. It covers Venus's habitable altitudes, floating balloon habitats, and the term surfacism.
gJ5KV3rzuag.why: HN links it in Mars-colonization threads as a concise case for Venus.

gM95HHI4gLk.summary: Salman Khan's TED 2011 talk on Khan Academy. He shows that it goes beyond video lectures to self-paced practice and analytics for teachers, and argues for filling gaps in understanding.
gM95HHI4gLk.why: HN recommends it to show Khan Academy's real model of mastery learning and teacher tools, often as a rebuttal to critics.

gMqZR3pqMjg.summary: Vox explains the Berlin and Kay research showing that languages around the world tend to invent color words in the same order. It walks through the hierarchy and the debate around it.
gMqZR3pqMjg.why: HN commenters recommend it as a clear, well-made summary of the linguistics of color naming and how culture shapes it.

gSKzgpt4HBU.summary: A PBS Space Time episode asking what matter, mass, and energy really are, starting with inertial versus gravitational mass and what mass-energy equivalence means.
gSKzgpt4HBU.why: HN recommends it, and the whole channel, as a clear and deeper-than-usual physics explainer.

ghUs-84NAAU.summary: Adam Neely tests the claims for tuning to A=432 Hz by trying the unusual tuning systems that its proponents' numerology requires. He compares how they sound against standard tuning and temperaments.
ghUs-84NAAU.why: HN points to it whenever the 432 Hz versus 440 Hz debate or tuning systems come up, and as an accessible entry point to music theory for non-musicians.

giQ8xEWjnBs.summary: Real Engineering explains why SpaceX is building Starlink, including the economics of satellite internet. It covers the latency advantage of light in vacuum over fiber for long-distance links.
giQ8xEWjnBs.why: Recommended as a clear explanation of Starlink's purpose and the case that it can beat fiber on latency for long routes.

gwvA49ZXnf8.summary: Bellingcat's publication of the recorded call in which Alexey Navalny, posing as a security aide, gets FSB officer Konstantin Kudryavtsev to describe the operation to poison him. It has English subtitles.
gwvA49ZXnf8.why: HN cites it as a striking confession obtained through caller ID spoofing and social engineering.

g6bOwQdCJrc.summary: Andrej Karpathy, then Tesla's head of AI, gives a CVPR 2021 workshop keynote on how Autopilot's neural networks work. A large part covers the move to a vision-only stack, including why radar was dropped and how vision produces depth estimates.
g6bOwQdCJrc.why: HN commenters cite it in Tesla threads as the primary-source explanation of why Tesla removed radar and how its vision depth estimation works.

gD_dZvPwAj0.summary: Comedian Dominic Frisby gives a ten-minute explanation of land value tax. He argues it would fix problems of rent-seeking and the economics of land ownership.
gD_dZvPwAj0.why: HN users share it as a short, accessible explainer for land value tax whenever housing, rents or inequality come up.

gFEE3w7F0ww.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Travis Oliphant, creator of NumPy, SciPy and Anaconda, about scientific Python and its history. It runs about three hours.
gFEE3w7F0ww.why: Recommended as a firsthand history of how Python became the language of scientific computing and ML.

gRRvjZ_XNog.summary: Filmmaker Max Joseph's 35-minute video essay asks whether you have to be a jerk to be a successful leader. It draws on Adam Grant's givers and takers, Robert Greene and famous demanding directors.
gRRvjZ_XNog.why: HN recommends it as a thoughtful critique of the great-leader-as-jerk myth in threads on difficult bosses.

gSKTfG1GXYQ.summary: Charlie Marsh of Astral explains how uv, a Rust Python package manager, got so fast. He covers allocators, concurrency, zero-copy tricks and the challenges of Python packaging.
gSKTfG1GXYQ.why: Recommended as a fascinating technical account of the optimizations behind uv's speed.

ggUduBmvQ_4.summary: A Wendover Productions explainer arguing that major airlines make much of their profit from loyalty programs and co-branded credit cards rather than flying. It frames airlines as quasi-banks that sell points in bulk, using United's pandemic-era loan as a hook.
ggUduBmvQ_4.why: HN commenters point to it whenever airline economics or frequent-flier miles come up, since it clearly shows loyalty programs are worth more than the airlines themselves.

giYbq4HmfGA.summary: José Valim's ElixirConf US 2023 closing keynote on the foundations of the Elixir type system, covering set-theoretic types and gradual typing with strong arrows.
giYbq4HmfGA.why: HN recommends it as the best detailed explanation from the language's creator of how Elixir's new type system works and why.

goePYJ74Ydg.summary: Primer simulates green beard altruism, where individuals recognize and help others carrying a shared marker, and shows how imposters affect its evolution. It is an animated evolution simulation based on published papers.
goePYJ74Ydg.why: HN recommends it as part of Primer's strong series of evolution and emergence simulations.

gqGEMQveoqg.summary: Van Jacobson's 2006 Google Tech Talk argues for rethinking networking around named data rather than host-to-host connections. He gives the history and the unsolved problems of the current internet architecture.
gqGEMQveoqg.why: Recommended as the foundational talk on content-centric and named-data networking, and for its internet history stories.

gsffg5xxFQI.summary: Derek Slager's Clojure/conj talk argues that ClojureScript is a pragmatic choice for web development. He addresses common objections, recent improvements, tooling and use cases where it shines.
gsffg5xxFQI.why: Recommended to JavaScript skeptics as a persuasive case for ClojureScript, covering Closure Compiler optimizations and code-splitting.

gDfNRWsMRsU.summary: Benn Jordan argues that Spotify's business model undermines the music it sells, using streaming payout figures and the economics for artists and labels.
gDfNRWsMRsU.why: Commenters recommend it as an artist's informed explanation of streaming economics and why Spotify pays so little compared with alternatives like Bandcamp.

gKWNjFagR9k.summary: Julien Verlaguet of Facebook describes applying static analysis and type inference to a very large PHP codebase, using OCaml. The work led to the Hack language.
gKWNjFagR9k.why: Pointed to as the origin story of Hack and a real-world example of OCaml in production.

gPlpphT7n9s.summary: David and Ben Crystal introduce the Original Pronunciation production of Shakespeare and show what it reveals about the history of English, including puns and rhymes lost in modern speech.
gPlpphT7n9s.why: Frequently linked as a short, accessible demonstration of how Shakespeare actually sounded.

gQnmP7UD_zk.summary: Huygens Optics experiments with etching tiny patterns in glass, covering hydrofluoric acid risks, buffered oxide etch, photoresist and chromium masks, and laser-induced etching. It ends with attempts at microscopic Tesla valves.
gQnmP7UD_zk.why: HN recommends it as a highly informative look at micro-etching glass and the smallest Tesla valves.

gSvUqhZcbVg.summary: A video essay explaining hauntology, Mark Fisher's idea of lost futures, and 80s nostalgia. It uses the Fallout games and other media as examples of a retro-futurism that mourns futures that never arrived.
gSvUqhZcbVg.why: Recommended as a clear introduction to hauntology and lost futures in discussions of Mark Fisher and cyberpunk.

gdK4y6O-llE.summary: Chuck Spinney, a long-time associate of John Boyd, presents Boyd's thinking on the OODA loop and evolutionary epistemology. The talk runs about two and a half hours and includes Q&A.
gdK4y6O-llE.why: HN readers recommend it as the way to learn what Boyd actually meant by OODA, straight from a collaborator, rather than from the popularized loop diagram.

ghtpJnrdgbo.summary: SQLite author Richard Hipp's talk at SouthEast LinuxFest criticizing Git's workflow and introducing Fossil as an alternative. He lists Git enhancements and argues for keeping history intact.
ghtpJnrdgbo.why: Recommended for the SQLite author's reasoned case for a different approach to version control, and as an introduction to Fossil.

gisdyTBMNyQ.summary: Tom Scott visits a rotating house near San Diego and explains how electricity, gas and water keep working on the rotating part. It includes a 3D render of the utility connection system.
gisdyTBMNyQ.why: HN likes the clear animation of how slip rings and piping let a house rotate.

goh2x_G0ct4.summary: Gil Scott-Heron's 1970 spoken-word piece, in an official audio upload. It contrasts the Apollo moon program with poverty and neglect at home.
goh2x_G0ct4.why: Posted in space-spending threads as a classic critique of priorities, usually with a quip.

gvZSpET11ZY.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on retirement plans, high fees and bad financial advice, with comedic sketches. It explains how fees eat into retirement savings and favors low-cost passive investing.
gvZSpET11ZY.why: HN links it in personal finance threads as an entertaining explanation of how fees erode retirement savings.

g0lrIi0ce5E.summary: A documentary about Riot Entertainment, a Finnish dot-com-era startup that raised millions in funding and then collapsed. It follows the hype-driven rise and implosion of the company.
g0lrIi0ce5E.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining dot-com-era story and a cautionary tale about VC funding and fake-it-till-you-make-it growth.

g1GgnbN9oNw.summary: A 2016 House Judiciary Committee hearing on encryption, held during the Apple and FBI iPhone dispute. It features testimony from Apple, the FBI and outside experts including Susan Landau, and runs over five hours.
g1GgnbN9oNw.why: HN users cite it as primary-source testimony, especially for the argument that weakening encryption is security versus security, not privacy versus security.

gLDYtH1RH-U.summary: A POV video of climbers illegally scaling the 650 m Shanghai Tower while it was under construction, filmed on a helmet camera.
gLDYtH1RH-U.why: HN recommends it as a gripping and vertigo-inducing watch that put rooftop climbers on the map.

gcS04BI2sbk.summary: Frederic Laloux presents his research on self-managing, purpose-driven organizations, followed by Q&A. He summarizes the findings of his book Reinventing Organizations and examples such as Buurtzorg.
gcS04BI2sbk.why: Recommended as the best introduction to self-management and new management paradigms.

ge7i60GuNRg.summary: A hidden-camera social experiment in a park where three people try to steal a bike in the open: a white teenager, a black teenager and a young woman. It records how bystanders react to each.
ge7i60GuNRg.why: Used in threads on bias and social engineering as a vivid example of how bystanders treat different thieves.

gn8m5d74fk8.summary: John Carmack's keynote at Oculus Connect 2014 about the Gear VR and development stories from building it. He discusses mobile GPU optimization, latency, and display ideas like programmable interlacing.
gn8m5d74fk8.why: HN recommends it for Carmack's detailed engineering insight into VR rendering and latency challenges.

gp4U5aH_T6A.summary: A long Lex Fridman podcast conversation with Austrian economist Saifedean Ammous, author of The Bitcoin Standard. They cover Bitcoin, fiat money, anarchy and Austrian economics.
gp4U5aH_T6A.why: Cited as a thorough statement of the bitcoin-maximalist case, with the host pushing back.

gC295d3V9gE.summary: Michael Arntzenius's Strange Loop talk on Datafun, a functional query language that brings database-style querying into a general-purpose language. It discusses bridging database theory and programming languages.
gC295d3V9gE.why: HN recommends it as an approachable talk on a total functional generalization of Datalog, by the language's author.

gTmhS6hcY-A.summary: A 2008 documentary by Brett Whitcomb about the Rock-afire Explosion, the animatronic band built for ShowBiz Pizza Place restaurants. It follows the band's history and the fans who keep the machines and their technology running.
gTmhS6hcY-A.why: HN commenters point to it whenever Chuck E. Cheese animatronics come up, as the best history of the band's direct ancestor and its devoted preservationists.

gUnxzVOs3rk.summary: ILM shows how The Mandalorian season one used a large curved LED wall to display interactive 3D environments in camera. The video covers the virtual production setup replacing location shoots.
gUnxzVOs3rk.why: Cited as the canonical look at LED-wall virtual production, referenced in threads on game engines in film and CGI.

gfh-VCTwMw8.summary: Jimmy Bogard presents a post-mortem of a real microservices migration that turned into a slow distributed monolith. He covers the modeling, development and production problems and how the team recovered.
gfh-VCTwMw8.why: Recommended as an entertaining cautionary talk on microservice failures and Conway's law.

ghDvyItIHTY.summary: Linus Tech Tips opens up an M1 MacBook Air to test whether better thermal pads could improve performance in the fanless design. It looks at what Apple left on the table.
ghDvyItIHTY.why: It is linked in laptop thermal threads for a layman's overview of why Apple limits surface temperature and why the mod is not simple.

gmn7tjSNyAA.summary: Researcher Kamal Meattle describes how an arrangement of three common houseplants placed in specific spots can measurably clean the air in a home or office. It is a short TED talk based on his work in a plant-filled building.
gmn7tjSNyAA.why: HN commenters cite it in threads about indoor air quality, CO2 and houseplants as a cheap, low-tech approach.

goSEyGNfiPM.summary: The US Chemical Safety Board's updated animation of the 2005 BP Texas City refinery explosion, which killed 15 workers. It was released ahead of a process safety training application.
goSEyGNfiPM.why: HN recommends the CSB's accident reconstruction animations as clear, worthwhile case studies of industrial disasters.

gtLxZiiuaXs.summary: WonderWhy surveys complex international borders, including enclaves like Vatican City, San Marino and Lesotho, the enclave-within-enclave town of Baarle, and the India-Bangladesh Cooch Behar region.
gtLxZiiuaXs.why: HN points to it as a visual explainer of enclaves, exclaves and counter-enclaves, especially in threads on the India-Bangladesh exchange.

g0TD0efcwVg.summary: Andrew Rota of Wayfair argues at React.js Conf 2015 that React and native Web Components complement each other. He shows how they can be combined for complex web applications.
g0TD0efcwVg.why: Cited in React versus Web Components threads as a clear picture of how the two interoperate and their challenges.

g0TaYhjpOfo.summary: An IEEE Spectrum compilation of humanoid robots falling over during the 2015 DARPA Robotics Challenge Finals.
g0TaYhjpOfo.why: HN uses it as the go-to illustration of Moravec's paradox and as a baseline for how far robotics has come since 2015.

g8JzXEoT9LI.summary: Essential Craftsman follows up on his earlier video about a DIY approach to sleep apnea. It centers on forcing nose breathing during sleep with mouth taping and nasal strips, and says to seek medical guidance.
g8JzXEoT9LI.why: HN people mention it as where they first heard of mouth taping and DIY CPAP-style fixes for sleep apnea.

gAjR4_CbPpQ.summary: The official music video for Daft Punk's Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger, taken from Discovery. It is a chapter of the anime film Interstella 5000 supervised by Leiji Matsumoto.
gAjR4_CbPpQ.why: Mostly used as a joke reference to the song's lyrics in AI threads, and cited for its robot-band theme in a thread about the song's tempo.

gORNmfpD0ak.summary: Eben Moglen's 2011 Personal Democracy Forum talk on the loss of anonymity and privacy on the internet. He proposes building an alternative net of personal servers, the idea behind FreedomBox.
gORNmfpD0ak.why: Cited in privacy and surveillance threads as an early argument for personal servers and decentralization.

gRelVFm7iJE.summary: A 39-minute highlights reel of Bill Gates being deposed by David Boies in the 1998 to 2001 United States v. Microsoft antitrust case.
gRelVFm7iJE.why: HN cites it as a view of Gates evading questions and sparring with a top lawyer.

gSrnXgAmK8k.summary: Linus Tech Tips documents a major RAID failure on its Whonnock server and the attempt to recover the lost data with a data recovery firm.
gSrnXgAmK8k.why: HN refers to it as an honest, candid account of the common story of losing precious data to storage failure.

ga_7j72CVlc.summary: A short clip from a 1973 NOVA episode in which Richard Feynman recalls his father teaching him that knowing the name of a bird in many languages tells you nothing about the bird.
ga_7j72CVlc.why: Reached for whenever a thread touches on naming versus actually understanding something.

gg40RWiaHRY.summary: Acerola explores building a shader that turns games into ASCII art, walking through techniques such as brightness mapping and edge detection to see whether it looks good.
gg40RWiaHRY.why: Pointed to as a nice overview of implementing ASCII rendering as a post-processing shader.

ggdYts4muu0.summary: A QCon London 2020 talk by Tesla engineers on the architecture of Tesla's Virtual Power Plant. It covers aggregating distributed batteries and solar with vertically integrated hardware and software across cloud and edge.
ggdYts4muu0.why: Cited as a technical look at how Tesla's VPPs and Autobidder work as distributed systems.

giAMt8Tj-84.summary: A 2006 Google TechTalk in which SQLite's author Richard Hipp introduces the embeddable, zero-configuration C database library. He covers its history, strengths and weaknesses, and where it beats client/server databases.
giAMt8Tj-84.why: Recommended as a first-hand intro from SQLite's creator that also teaches how a database engine is built.

gocwRvLhDf8.summary: Tom Scott explains YouTube's 11-character video IDs, which are base-64 encoded 64-bit numbers, and whether YouTube could ever run out of them. It covers counting systems and base 64 briefly.
gocwRvLhDf8.why: HN links it whenever IDs, base64 or random identifier space come up, as a short and pleasant explainer.

gp0FI8Gw1iA.summary: A long personal account by a former NixOS contributor of his experience in the community, his ban and the governance events. He aims to correct what he sees as a false narrative about the NixOS drama.
gp0FI8Gw1iA.why: Linked as a firsthand account of the NixOS moderation and governance disputes, from a banned member's perspective.

gzgyksS5pX8.summary: Jim Keller, CTO of Tenstorrent, gives a keynote at Stanford's System X conference on change, understanding and the future of computing. He touches on Moore's Law, how far transistors are from physical limits, and ideas like DNA origami.
gzgyksS5pX8.why: HN commenters cite it as a thoughtful talk from a legendary chip architect, both for the s-curves view of progress and for concrete technical details on semiconductor scaling.

g0amdIcZt5I.summary: Veritasium visits the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory to see the world's strongest magnets and demonstrate effects like eddy currents. It covers what intense magnetic fields do to materials and objects.
g0amdIcZt5I.why: Cited as a reference for magnet safety, eddy currents and superconductor levitation in physics threads.

g1Sq1Nr58hM.summary: A very short clip of Tim Curry from Red Alert 3, captioned as escaping to space. It is a meme-style video clip.
g1Sq1Nr58hM.why: Mostly posted as a joke in threads about capitalism, SpaceX and Red Alert.

g1VEwsI4SlY.summary: BBC Earth shows killer whales working as a pod to create waves that wash seals off ice floes, with the producer explaining how the crew captured behavior once thought a myth.
g1VEwsI4SlY.why: Cited as a striking example of coordinated hunting and intelligence in orcas.

gBCUQlF3MMU.summary: Coast Guard footage of a Cirrus SR-22 pilot who ran out of fuel over the Pacific and deployed the airframe parachute, then escaped into a life raft. It shows the Cirrus Airframe Parachute System working in a real emergency.
gBCUQlF3MMU.why: Linked in aviation threads as a concrete example of the Cirrus parachute in action, including its rough touchdown.

gBE6glZNJuU.summary: A compilation of Terry A. Davis, creator of TempleOS, ranting about Linus Torvalds and operating systems. It is an archived video from his old channel.
gBE6glZNJuU.why: Cited as Terry Davis in his purest form, and for his analogy of what an OS is to its user.

gBVuAGFcGKY.summary: An SNL skit featuring Tom Brady in a mock workplace training video on sexual harassment, where the difference between welcome and unwelcome advances depends on who makes them. It is a satirical sketch.
gBVuAGFcGKY.why: Brought up humorously in threads about harassment and gender discrimination as satire that makes the point.

gCKhktcbfQM.summary: A very short clip from Taken 3 of Liam Neeson's character jumping a fence, edited with extremely rapid cuts.
gCKhktcbfQM.why: Used as a stock example of overly fast cutting and shaky-cam action filmmaking.

gCMzjJjuxQI.summary: A one-minute 1949 television commercial for Camel cigarettes claiming that more doctors smoke Camels than any other cigarette.
gCMzjJjuxQI.why: HN cites it as a historical example of corporations using doctors and misleading advertising, drawing analogies to modern industries.

gE8ZikfrpFU.summary: A profane video review in the Your Product Sucks series that picks apart the Apple Music app on macOS Catalina and its usability problems.
gE8ZikfrpFU.why: HN cites it, with schadenfreude, as evidence that Apple Music on desktop is poorly built.

gECj1AE9D2c.summary: A short project video in which Greg Raiz turns a 32-inch eInk display into a wireless digital newspaper showing daily front pages. It runs for months on battery, and the code is published on GitHub.
gECj1AE9D2c.why: HN commenters cite it as inspiration for large eInk displays and their own DIY projects.

gEDaCIDvj6I.summary: A kiai master offers a 5000 dollar challenge that he can beat any MMA fighter, and his supposed energy techniques have no effect on the fighter.
gEDaCIDvj6I.why: It is cited as an example of mystical or energy-based martial arts failing against real fighters, alongside the Tai Chi master incident.

gEwDImE0DU4.summary: Ben Heck modifies a keyboard with magnets, Hall effect sensors and an Xbox controller so the WASD keys give analog control. He walks through the hardware build.
gEwDImE0DU4.why: Cited as 2012 prior art for analog keyboards when newer analog-key products and patents come up.

gEyFH-a-XoQ.summary: An Onion News Network satire about Prague's Kafka International being ranked the most alienating airport because of delays, bureaucratic staff, and an oppressive atmosphere.
gEyFH-a-XoQ.why: Posted as a joke whenever Kafkaesque bureaucracy comes up, and several commenters call it a favorite Onion video.

gGYoeJ5U7cQ.summary: A two-minute video compiled by the War on Fear channel about the Chinese government's treatment of Uyghurs in Xinjiang. It includes footage of detainees being moved onto trains.
gGYoeJ5U7cQ.why: HN commenters cite it as footage evidence of detainee transport in Xinjiang during threads about the camps and forced labor.

gJJH7a2J9O8.summary: ElixirConf EU 2023 talk by Giuseppe Castagna and Guillaume Duboc on bringing set-theoretic types to Elixir, and the benefits such a type system could offer such as catching bugs.
gJJH7a2J9O8.why: Linked as the authoritative background on how Elixir's gradual set-theoretic type system works.

gLcWfecmZhE.summary: Nick Lane's Royal Institution lecture on the origin of life and why it is the way it is. It draws on his book The Vital Question and the alkaline hydrothermal vent theory of abiogenesis.
gLcWfecmZhE.why: HN points to it as an accessible presentation of Lane's ideas on life's origins and the rarity of complex life.
